key_insight: Finite-element-guided patterning of a silicon nitride stressor layer can shape a silicon crystal into a near-sinusoidal crystalline undulator with nanometer-scale amplitude and sub-millimeter period.
engineering_relevance: This enables fabrication of compact crystal-based gamma-ray sources for 5–30 GeV beams, with potential use in advanced radiation and particle-beam applications.
method: Simulated substrate/stressor geometry with FEM to target sinusoidal deformation
Optimized substrate thickness and undulator period to suppress higher harmonics
Fabricated a 160 μm-thick device with 10 periods and 334 μm pitch
evidence_signal: The fabricated device showed structural integrity and a uniform deformation extending up to 20 μm from the surface, with design targets aimed at >1 nm amplitude.
watch_item: Performance depends on maintaining highly uniform deformation; residual higher harmonics or fabrication tolerances could reduce undulator quality and radiation output.
paper_title: From Simulation to Fabrication: Realizing Silicon Crystalline Undulators with Silicon Nitride Stressor Layer Patterning
